articleTitle: Investigation on Beam Scanning Speed of Hybrid Leaky-Wave Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Application
abstract: A hybrid asymmetric folded substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) and spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) combined waveguiding structure is employed to design a dual-band frequency-scanning leaky-wave antenna with slower beam scanning speed at forward region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(30^{\mathrm{o}} < \theta < 62^{\mathrm{o}})$</tex> and faster beam scanning speed at backward region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-56^{\mathrm{o}} < \theta < -18^{\mathrm{o}})$</tex> specifically. The waveguide structure is obtained by cutting a vertical AFSIW in half along its longitudinal symmetrical plane and adding SSPP structure along one side of middle copper layer of AFSIW. The n = 0 dominant mode remains at lower frequency band and the n = -1 space harmonic mode is generated effectively by sinusoidal modulation.

articleTitle: A D-Band Energy-Efficient Compact Receiver with Current Reuse Technique for 6G Array System
abstract: This paper presents a 140GHz zero-IF receiver for terahertz array systems using TSMC 40nm CMOS process. On the one hand, the currents of the active mixer and the low-noise amplifier are partially multiplexed, while the currents of the oscillator and the frequency multiplier are fully reused, in order to reduce the power consumption. On the other hand, the compact layout design allows a receiver area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.4 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex> (including pads). Simulation results show that the receiver achieves an SSB NF of 11.2dB and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{IP}_{\mathrm{l}\mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}}$</tex> of −13.8dBm, with 10dB conversion gain and 10GHz bandwidth, while requiring only 48mW of power consumption.

articleTitle: Design of A Four-Channel Crossover in Ridge- Gap-Waveguide Technology for Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel four-channel crossover is proposed utilizing ridge-gap-waveguide (RGW) technology, which can address the crossing of four channels simultaneously. The RGW structure employs air as the medium, contributing to low dielectric loss. The simulated results display that the minimum insertion loss is 0.52dB, the reflection and isolation coefficients are less than −15dB from 27.8 GHz to 28.3 GHz with 28 GHz as the center frequency.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Wide-Angle Scanning Antenna Array Using Heterogeneous Metasurface Elements with Ability of Integrating Millimeter-Wave Array
abstract: This manuscript presents a novel heterogeneous antenna array with merits of high isolation and wide-angle scanning operated in Sub-6GHz, which can integrate millimeter-wave (mmW) array in same aperture. Firstly, two kinds of metasurface antennas including square ring metasurface (SRMS) and overlapped metasurface (MS) are proposed, and they are used as heterogeneous elements to construct a scanning array. The overlapped MS significantly minimizes the size of the element. The square ring metasurface antenna exhibits a larger height and high transparency at mmW, in order to provide enough space for mmW antennas. Note that, the different height of the heterogeneous antennas have different phase centers, therefore, an 60° delay microstrip is designed into the feeding network ensuring the phase consistency. To further improve the isolation and scanning performance of the array, some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> -shaped decoupling-path and dummy elements are loaded around the array. As result, the array can operate at 3.3-3.6GHz with high isolation that larger than 19.5dB. In addition, it also can achieve a wide-angle scanning performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-56^{\circ}\sim 56^{\circ}$</tex> in the whole band. These results reveal that the proposed heterogeneous array would be potentially applied in mmW/Sub-6GHz aperture-shared arrays.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Decoupling Method for Millimeter-Wave High-Isolation Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Antenna
abstract: A novel dual-band decoupling method is proposed and applied to millimeter-wave phased array for wide-angle scanning. By introducing comb-shaped branch, “I”-shaped branch and grounded vias simultaneously, two kinds of extra decoupling paths are generated to cancel the inherent couplings at two frequencies, respectively, thus achieving dual-band decoupling. To verify the decoupling structure, a broadband magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is designed, ranging from 24.13 to 45.17 GHz (60.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), which can cover the main 5G operating frequency bands of 24.25-29.5 GHz and 37-43.5 GHz. Then, the two decoupling structures are loaded on the lx4 antenna array. The isolations between all the elements in both the two operating bands are greater than 20 dB, and compared with the array without decoupling structures, the isolations are improved by at least 5 dB. Benefited from the dual-band decoupling, the scanning range can cover from −64° to 63° in the low frequency band nearby 28GHz, with a gain fluctuation of 2.4 dB, meanwhile the array at high frequency band nearby 40GHz can scan up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 48^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex>, with a gain fluctuation less than 3 dB. Besides, the proposed method can be expectedly applied in larger scale array.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Communication
abstract: A broadband dual-polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented for millimeter-wave communication. Two orthogonal feeding networks, utilizing cross aperture coupling, are implemented for vertical and horizontal polarization. In addition, a metallized blind-via is introduced to extend the operating band. Consequently, an overlapped impedance bandwidth of 26.76-39.66 GHz (38.8%) is obtained.

articleTitle: Accurate Noncontact Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Detection using a K-band Biomedical Radar
abstract: The golden standard of nocturnal respiratory function assessment is polysomnography (PSG) especially for diagnosis of sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (SAHS). However, the use of PSG sensors usually obstructs the patients' breathing, causing discomfort. One of the most important signals in PSG to assess respiratory function is airflow, especially for sleep apnea detection. Radar-based contactless detection technique provides a non-contact monitor way to overcome such limitation. Aiming at developing an alternative of airflow, a 24-GHz biomedical radar sensor combined with airflow reconstruction algorithm is developed to provide accurate continuous measurement of respiratory waveform during sleep. Simultaneously with PSG, the radar data of SAS patients were recorded to validate the monitoring feasibility of the sleep apnea-hypopnea events, which consists of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), central sleep apnea (CSA) and hypopnea. The overnight experimental results show that all the apnea and hypopnea events can be accurately detected, which makes the at-home monitoring possible in the future.

articleTitle: Wide-Scanning Reflector-Based Holographic Metasurfaces with Open-Stopband Suppression
abstract: In this article, a wide-scanning reflector-based holographic metasurface with open-stopband suppression is proposed for microwave and millimeter-wave applications. By employing a parabolic reflector and using a nonuniform proportional modulation method, the gain bandwidth and aperture efficiency are simultaneously improved. Moreover, anisotropic holographic metasurface is proposed to suppress the open-stopband (OSB) issue. In this case, the reflection coefficient and antenna gain no longer deteriorate rapidly when the beams scan through the broadside, and thus obtaining a wide beam coverage including the elevation angle of zero degree. The measurement results show that the isotropic holographic metasurface achieves a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 39.2% and a maximum aperture efficiency of 30.2%, while the anisotropic design achieves a simulated 3-dB gain bandwidth of 36% and a maximum aperture efficiency of 35.9%. The proposed metasurface features low cost, high gain, wide scanning range, and planar integration, which is a good candidate for multi-point energy transfer or beam scanning applications.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction for Machine Learning-Based Alignment of W-band Higher-Order Mode Generator
abstract: This paper proposes methods of extracting features from simulation data for use in machine learning models to optimize the alignment of the W-band mode generator. We introduce the Scalar Cor-relation Factor (SCF) and Mean Square Error (MSE) as methods for comparing fields to quantify the field data used as features. These methods are validated using Deep Neural Networks (DNN) to predict mode generator misalignments for effective optimization. The two feature extraction methods are compared based on simulation and experimental results, revealing that SCF demonstrates outstanding accuracy in predictions.

articleTitle: A GaN-based Doherty Power Amplifier for 5G Basestation Applications
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficient and linear Doherty power amplifier targeting base station applications for the fifth-generation (5G) communication systems. With the adoption of self-packaged <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.25-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> GaN/SiC high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), a quasi-Doherty power amplifier (P A) featuring an operating frequency from 3.4-3.6 GHz was realized. The fabricated P A delivered a saturated output power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}})$</tex> of 50.5 dBm, and a peak power-added-efficiency (P AE) of 60.6% while excited by continuous-wave (CW) signal at 3.5 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Fabry-Pérot Antenna Featuring Frequency Reconfigurable Capability
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique for realizing a frequency-reconfigurable Fabry-Pérot cavity (FPC) antenna utilizing polarization standing waves (PSWs) and metasurfaces. The antenna's operating frequency can be continuously adjusted within a range of 60.8 - 66.2 GHz, providing versatility for various communication applications. The integration of metasurfaces enables precise control over the electromagnetic field distribution, resulting in a high boresight gain of 22.2 dBi. The experimental demonstration of the proposed antenna at 60 GHz validates the effectiveness of the design approach.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Fall Detection System Based on Finite Human Node Scattering Model
abstract: With the rapid development of the aging population, radar-based fall detection has become a research hotspot in the field of health monitoring. In this paper, a fall detection method based on the human motion scattering model is proposed to enhance the accuracy of fall detection and address the issue of challenging data acquisition. Specifically, the kinematics model of the human body is described, and the radar backscattering model under human motion is established. Simulation research and analysis of human micro-Doppler characteristics are conducted to analyze the correlation between the characteristic micro-Doppler information and body parts when the human body is walking and falling. This analysis aims to simplify the backscattering model of human radar and enhance detection efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate that the method effectively reduces the probability of false alarm and missing alarm.

articleTitle: A Dual- Polarized Metalens with Wide Field-of- View and Broad Bandwidth for 77GHz Radar Applications
abstract: This research introduces a novel approach to designing a dual-polarized metalens that exhibits wide field-of-view (FOV) with a broad bandwidth (71–87 GHz). The metalens is composed of three metallic layers, with an ultra-thin thick-ness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.13\lambda_{c}$</tex>, and a large numerical aperture (NA=0.707). To address the off-axis aberration, we design a wide FOV metalens with two types of unit cells and an optimized polynomial phase profile. To validate our approach, a dual-polarized metalens with a diameter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\lambda_{c}$</tex> is designed and simulated. The simulation results demonstrate that the metal ens achieves high focusing efficiencies, tight focal spot sizes (Strel Ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 0.75$</tex>) and low sidelobe levels (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq-10dB$</tex>) across a wide angular range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[-45^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}]$</tex>. The proposed dual-polarized metalens holds promising potential for applications of millimeter-wave radars.

articleTitle: 94 GHz Two-Way-Combined Power Amplifiers with 14.2 dBm Peak Output Power in 300-nm InP/GaAsSb DHBT Technology
abstract: We present two-way-combined Power Amplifiers (PAs) in 300-nm InP/GaAsSb DHBT technology. One-Stage Common-Base (CB) and Common-Emitter (CE) structures are used as PA cells. The comparison between the two exhibits that the former delivers higher output power and superior gain compression behavior. At 94 GHz, class-ABbiased CB-based PA achieves 14.2 dBm POUT, SAT and 10.6% PAE. POUT, SAT at 92-96 GHz stays in the 13.9-14.3 dBm range. The technology used in this work features the highest maximum oscillation frequency fMAX = 1.2 THz in any bipolar transistor, record POUT, SAT, and power density per unit emitter area in any InP HBT, making GaAsSb-based DHBTs well-suited for mm- and sub-mm-wave power amplification. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first PA reported in InP/GaAsSb HBT technology exploiting the aforementioned advantages in mm-wave PAs.

articleTitle: Nano-Scale Rough Surface Imaging with THz-s-SNOM
abstract: Terahertz scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (THz-s-SNOM), known for its high resolution, is widely used across fields. However, its application to sample shapes is underexplored. This study simulates rough surfaces, revealing the impact of surface roughness on scattered signals. Using a self-built THz-s-SNOM system, it images contaminated samples, aiding in determining surface contaminant nature. These findings enhance our understanding of sample morphology effects on THz-s-SNOM signals, showcasing its diverse applications. The study emphasizes the need for further exploration and technological advancements to improve practical utility.

articleTitle: A 55 GHz Single-Stage RC Polyphase Filter with LC Matching Network for Low Insertion Loss
abstract: This paper presents a 55GHz single-stage RC polyphase filter (PPF) with LC matching network to reduce insertion loss. In the millimeter-wave frequency, PPF has high insertion loss. To reduce the insertion loss, this paper proposes a PPF with LC matching network connected to the input/output ports. The measured result of insertion loss was 17.4 dB for the 4-port average and image rejection ratio (IRR) was 19.2 dB at 55 GHz. The phase error was −4 to 4.4° at 55 GHz and −10.8 to 12.6° in the 50 to 60 GHz range and the amplitude error with respect to the I port was −1.85 to −0.75 dB at 55 GHz and −2.0 to −0.37 dB in the 50 to 60 GHz range. This PPF is fabricated using a 40-nm CMOS process and has an area of 0.45 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads and a core area including the matching network of 0.12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Directional Interpolation Pattern for Multilevel Green's Function Interpolation Method
abstract: Multilevel Green's function interpolation method (MLGFIM) is a fast numerical method whose computational complexity is O(N log N). Since MLGFIM is based on interpolation techniques, the efficiency of MLGFIM is highly associated with the number of interpolation points. To improve the efficiency of MLGFIM, a directional interpolation pattern for decreasing the required number of interpolation points is proposed. With the directional interpolation pattern, the number of interpolation points in the tangent directions can be decreased because the phase in the tangent direction oscillates mush mildly than that in the radial direction. As a result, the total required number of interpolation points decreases and the efficiency of MLGFIM improves.

articleTitle: Integrated Circuits of RF Front-End with Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Receiver
abstract: This article presents millimeter-wave integrated on-chip antenna with bandpass filter, double balanced mixer and low noise amplifier are fabricated with tsmc CMOS technology. The on-chip dipole with balun of the antenna adopts via-hole structure and SIR pseudo-interdigital bandpass filter utilizes. The proposed integrated on-chip antenna-bandpass filter and low noise amplifier can be very useful for the millimeter-wave integrated design of the 60-GHz CMOS radio-frequency receiver.

articleTitle: A 18-to-22 GHz 22.8 dBm PSAT 18.2 dB Gain Power Amplifier in 0.13-μm CMOS SOI
abstract: This paper presents a 18-22 GHz stacked power amplifier (PA) in 0.13-μm CMOS SOI technology. The amplifier adopts cascode unit topology, and utilizes twoway power combining networks to improve the output power. Neutralization capacitor is customized in the design to enhance the stability and in-band gain flatness. The PA achieves a small-signal gain of 18.2dB and 3-dB bandwidth (BW) of 10 GHz, a 1-dB compressed power (P1dB) of 18.2 dBm and a saturated output power (PSAT) of 22.8 dBm with a peak PAE of 29.0%. The PA chip area is 0.44 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including the pads.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Three-Way Coupler Based on Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
abstract: A three-way coupler based on ridge gap waveguide (RGW) technology is proposed, which can be applied to the construction of beamforming networks such as Butler matrices. Meanwhile, benefiting from the employment of RGW, the design bears the characteristics of low loss. Within the working frequency from 27.50 GHz to 28.34 GHz, the design enables the trisection of power at the output ports. A constant phase difference of –120°, 0° and 120° can be realized when the input port is excited, respectively. The reflections and isolation coefficients of each port are all lower than –15 dB. The three-way coupler has a wide application prospect in 5G applications for working in the frequency of millimeter-wave.

articleTitle: 2D-Scalable CMOS Phased Array Transmitter at 140GHz with λ/2 Element Spacing
abstract: This article demonstrates a 140GHz phased array transmitter in a half-wavelength layout in both dimensions. The 4x4 phased array is composed of multiple 2x2 chips and can expand the array in the 2D direction, up to a maximum of 10^3 array elements. It realizes long-distance communication> 15m, and the real-time communication rate reaches 1Gbps. The chip is manufactured using TSMC 65nm bulk CMOS process, which can be applied to future large-scale terahertz phased array systems at low cost.

articleTitle: A Wideband Monostatic Co-Circularly Polarized Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Antenna Using Metasurface
abstract: A wideband mono static metasurface-based simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna system with high isolation and co-circularly polarized (Co-CP) radiation is proposed. The STAR antenna consists of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> dual-polarized metasurface (DPMS) antenna array shared by TX and RX for mono static operation. To achieve high TXlRX isolation and identical right-handed CP (RHCP), the four TX and RX ports of the STAR antenna are excited with equal amplitudes and relative phases of 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270°, respectively, by using two wideband integrated feeding networks. Measured results show that the proposed STAR antenna system achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 36\text{dB}$</tex> TXlRX isolation and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 3\text{dB}$</tex> axial ratio from 4.5 to 6 GHz, and maintains similar radiation patterns with the same RHCP for TX and RX.

articleTitle: A Broadband Millimeter-Wave Antenna-in-Package Made of Low-Profile Magnetoelectric Dipole
abstract: This paper presents a broadband millimeter-wave planar magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna. By intro-ducing an E-shaped feeding branch underneath the main radiating patch, a broadband ME dipole antenna with an ultra-low profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.086\lambda_{0}$</tex> (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> represents the free-space) is obtained. A simulated impedance bandwidth of 19.3% (23.4-28.4 GHz) is obtained from the proposed antenna. Across the impedance bandwidth, the ME dipole also shows good radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: A 17.7-21.2 GHz Antenna Element for SATCOM Phased-Array Receiver
abstract: This article presents a wideband scalable 17.7-20.2 GHz antenna element for satellite communication (SAT-COM) phased-array receiver. The microstrip stacked-patch antenna uses an annular feeding network and two cross-shaped integrated slots and is able to receive two circularly polarized waves. A dual-layer metasurface configuration, in-cluding a 4 × 4 patch superimposed with a 2 × 2 patch, is used as the radiating patch and achieve wideband impedance matching. The enclosed metallic wall and vias are used to improve the isolation among array elements. Simulations confirm the wide bandwidth, lower feed coupling (> 12.6 dB), wide 3-dB beamwidth (~82°), minimal cross-polarization (> 19 dB), wide axial ratio versus scan angle (±700), and high port-to-port isolation (> 14.5 dB). The 1024-element array's radiation pattern simulations have validated its low sidelobes (~13.5 dB), and the array can scan to ±70° in all planes without grating lobes.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Staggered Double Vane Structure with Bragg Resonators for 200 GHz TWT
abstract: This research introduces a methodology for designing a staggered double-vane (SDV) traveling-wave tube (TW7) optimized for efficient operation at 200 GHZ. The two- stage structure ejg'ectively suppresses backward beam-wave interaction and generates a stable output signaL By conducting particle-in-cell simulation, it is observed that the proposed structure generates ejg'ective beam-wave interaction and has a gain of 33. 51 dB at 20 ns.

articleTitle: Indoor Stationary Human Detection and Localization Based on FMCW Radar
abstract: This paper utilizes millimeter-wave radar as a non-contact sensing device for detecting and positioning stationary living bodies. The choice of radar is motivated by good privacy, and the system components required to process millimeter-wave signals are small in size and easy to integrate. Specifically, a 60GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar is employed, leveraging its multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) modes for accurate target localization. The proposed method determines the presence of living things based on dispersion entropy (DE) and energy ratio values, using density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) for target counting. The approach involves preprocessing the echo signal, calculating DE and energy ratio, and utilizing these indicators for human detection. The Range-Azimuth (RA) map is then derived, and cluster analysis is performed on high-energy areas to identify the number and location of targets. After sliding window analysis of each set of data, the detection accuracy exceeds 97%.

articleTitle: Broadband GaN MMIC Asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifier Employing Complex Load Impedance
abstract: This work presents the design and simulation of a broadband fully integrated asymmetric Doherty power amplifier (ADPA) that employs complex combining load impedance, the continuous operation is achieved at both output power back-off (OBO) point and saturation. A 250-nm gallium nitride (GaN) process was used in this design. The impedance inverter network (lIN) and post-matching network (PMN) were implemented using lumped components, furthermore, the parasitic parameters of transistors are also absorbed into the matching network to simplify the matching structure. Within the working frequency band of 4.3-5.1 GHz, the simulation results shows that the saturated drain efficiency (DE) of the designed DPA is between 58.9%-61.3%, with a saturated output power of 39.4-40.3 dBm. 46.7%-52.0% DE is achieved at 8 dB OBO within the working bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reconfigurable Reflective Metasurface
abstract: This paper presents a novel 1-bit reconfigurable reflective metasurface design that achieves wide impedance bandwidth for potential integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) applications. A dual-patch unit cell with a pin diode is proposed to realize two reflection states with 180° phase difference. Analysis based on equivalent circuit shows that the pin diode acts as an inductor and capacitor in the “ON” and “OFF” states, respectively. Full-wave simulations validate that the metasurface exhibits a 1-bit phase modulation between 15.5-27.5 GHz, corresponding to a 55.8% relative impedance bandwidth. Furthermore, an 18x18 metasurface array is simulated and a 39.1 % 3-dB gain bandwidth is achieved. Its wideband and reconfigurable features make it a potential solution for ISAC applications such as high-resolution radar imaging and sensing.

articleTitle: Determination of Orbital Angular Momentum Modes With Double Slit Experiments in W-band
abstract: We introduce a method for identifying Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) modes in the millimeter wave range, especially in high-power environments where direct phase measurements are challenging. Instead of relying on phase measurements, the proposed method utilizes intensity measurements based on the asymmetric phase patterns of OAM beams. This approach involves using a Young's double slit interference setup to discern OAM modes, introducing the gyrotron-based OAM mode identification. We present simulation results and experimental results in low power, and compare with experimental result in high power.

articleTitle: An Accuracy Improving Method of Error Vector Magnitude Measurement System for 78 GHz Broadband Modulated Signals
abstract: With the high-speed development of millimetrewave (mmW) communication, the mmW signal transmission quality problem has received corresponding attention. Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) is a crucial parameter to measure signal transmission quality, which is an important index to evaluate whether the communication system is reliable. In our previous work, the author proposed a method for measuring EVM parameters of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}$</tex>-band communication signals based on electro-optic sampling (EOS). This method avoids introducing additional nonlinear distortions and solves the problem of vector signal analyzers being unable to measure highfrequency broadband-modulated signals. Based on our previous work, this paper estimates the channel characteristics of the measurement system and performs postprocessing on the received measurement signal using the estimated results to obtain more accurate measurements. The experimental results indicate that the EVM of the 78 GHz signal is 24.41% @1 GBaud, which is reduced to 9.8%@1 GBaud after channel estimation. This improvement demonstrates the feasibility of the channel estimation correction method.

articleTitle: Terahertz Plasmonic Instability of a Double-layer Two-dimensional Electron System
abstract: Solid-state on-chip radiation devices based on plasmonic waves of two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs) have vast application prospects in terahertz (THz) band. In this work, we adopt a hydrodynamic model to analyze the mechanism of the THz plasmonic wave excitation in a double-layer 2DEG system, where the electron drift velocity exists only in one 2DEG layer and the other is static. The result shows that the plasmonic instability occurs when the Doppler shifted slow wave in the drifted 2DEG layer synchronizes with the forward wave in the static 2DEG layer. To explore the principal rules guiding the device design, the critical factors that influencing the wave frequency and growth rate are also discussed, including the effects of the convection velocity, the electron densities, and the dielectric thicknesses.

articleTitle: On The Use of 3D Printing Technique for 5G mmWave Antenna Development
abstract: This paper discusses the use of additive manufacturing technology, more commonly known as 3D printing, in the fabrication of antennas for fifth-generation (5G) communications in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) spectrum. The 3D printing technology holds great promise in the manufacturing of radio frequency (RF)/microwave components and is particularly suitable for producing mmWave components such as antennas. Here, the proposed antenna takes a rectangular patch with the dielectric substrate made of acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) material and manufactured using 3D printing technique Whilst its conductive parts are coated by nickel conductive paint. Measurement results indicate that the manufactured antenna can operate within the frequency range of 24.6 GHz to 27.8 GHz with the maximum gain of 4.4 dBi.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Effective Degree of Freedom for Multiport Antenna Element
abstract: The multiple-input and multiple-output performance of multiport antenna element is investigated based on a three-port antenna. Both anechoic chamber and reverberation chamber are used to simulate line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight scenarios, respectively. It is demonstrated that the peak effective degree of freedom (EDoF) for the threeport antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50{{\% }}$</tex> higher than that of dual-polarized antenna, which can only be achieved at higher SNR region, especially for line-of-sight scenarios. Moreover, when the SNR is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20{{\ dB}}$</tex>, the EDoF of the three-port antenna is only slightly higher than dual-polarized antenna in anechoic chamber, whereas the EDoF of the three-port antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$36{{\% }}$</tex> higher than DP antenna in reverberation chamber.

articleTitle: Filtenna-to-Filtenna-Based Frequency Selective Surfaces With Improved Performances
abstract: Two kinds of frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) based on Filtenna-To-Filtenna (FA-T-FA) structures with improved performances are presented in this paper, including Filtenna-Filtenna and Filtenna-Filter-Filtenna structures. The FA-FA one consists of two back-to-back filtennas. Wide transmission bandwidth and two stop bands are obtained. Compared with FA-FA FSS, a filter-embedded ground plane is introduced between two filtennas, forming FA-F-FA FSS. A wider passband and rejection band can be achieved.

articleTitle: Electronically Controlled 1-Bit Reconfigurable Broadband Circular-Polarized Reflective Metasurface
abstract: This paper proposes an electrically controlled, broadband, 1-bit circular-polarized reconfigurable reflective metasurface. By altering the feeding state of the active elements, the equivalent structure is changed, resulting in a 1-bit circular-polarized phase difference. The element has a stable 180° phase shift and a good reflection coefficient in the range of 6.82-9.96GHz (37% relative bandwidth). The fabricated 8×8 metasurface sample achieves circular-polarized wave control at least from 7.4 to 9.9GHz. The proposed reconfigurable metasurface provides a promising application for electromagnetic wave manipulation.

articleTitle: Compact Multibeam Antenna Fed by Dual-Layer Substrate Integrated Waveguide Butler Matrix for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
abstract: A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> multibeam array antenna centered at 26 GHz fed by a compact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 \times 4$</tex> Butler matrix is designed and manufactured in dual-layer substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. This proposed configuration avoids two crossovers and two phase shifters in conventional designs, and therefore significantly reduces the overall size. In addition, wideband phase shifters are designed to enable a flat phase characteristic. The experimental results show a 15.4% impedance bandwidth from 24 to 28 GHz. The measured maximum gain achieves 10.4 dBi, and the 3-dB beam width covers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 63^{\circ}$</tex>. Its good performance indicates the potential for 5G millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Studies of Beam-Squinting Effects Between Leaky-Wave and Phased Array Antennas
abstract: This paper is dedicated to comparing the similarities and differences between leaky-wave antennas (L WAs) and phased array antennas (P AAs) regarding their beam-squinting effects. It is shown that although a general L W A and phase-shifter-based P AA suffer from a narrow instantaneous bandwidth due to the common issue of beam-squinting, the specific behaviors of their beams as frequency varies are different. In particular, the useful radiation frequency band of an L W A presents a spatial dependence, whereas this phenomenon is not possessed by a phase-shifter-based P AA. On the other hand, it is observed that the time-delay circuits/devices that are usually deployed in wideband P AAs can be properly implemented in L W As to design a class of wide band LWAs featuring fixed-beam radiation. From the authors' perspective, such a comparative study can help general readers grasp basic yet important pictures concerning the frequency- and phase-based beam-scanning architectures.

articleTitle: Terahertz Spoof Plasmonic Sensor with Resonance Sensing Capability for Wood Moisture Detection
abstract: Exact detection of moisture content is essential to preserve the quality of wood, since it can stop swelling and shrinkage. This paper proposes a theory based on the interaction between spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) and spoof localized surface plasmon (SLSPs) for the purpose of detecting moisture content in wood utilizing a planar terahertz sensor structure. The numerous resonance frequencies generated by this sensor are used to detect moisture content by measuring variations in the shift of these resonance frequencies within a designated operating band. When the standard block is fixed, the simulated results show that the sensor has a fix resonance frequency. Conversely, if the moisture in the wood being tested is higher than that of the standard block, resonance frequencies move towards lower frequencies, suggesting that the proposed method works well for screening wood that does not match moisture content standards. The topic of wood processing can benefit from the practical applications of this research. Furthermore, these results provide a path toward the development of planar spoof plasmonic devices into useful sensors in the terahertz regime.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave 3D Printing High-Gain Shorted Patch Antenna With Enhanced Bandwidth
abstract: A 3D printing shorted microstrip antenna with high gain in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band is come up with in this article. The proposed mmWave microstrip antenna is made up of a shorted rectangular metal radiator, ground plane and a substrate integrated coaxial-line (SICL) feeding network. Therefore, the dielectric loss is reduced compared to printed circuit board technics. In addition, the radiating patch is excited through a rectangular coupling slot perforating the metal ground plane. Besides, both the coupling slot and the shorted rectangular patch contribute to the low cross polarization. As indicated by simulation results, the antenna operating band spans from 36 to 40 GHz, achieving a peak gain of 10.1 dBi and a cross-polarization level of below -20 dB.

articleTitle: A Single-Channel Detection Method with Multi-Order Matched Filters for Wideband Linear Frequency Modulation Harmonic Signals
abstract: In this paper, a single-channel detection method for wideband linear frequency modulation(LFM) signal with multi-order matched filters is proposed. The extraction moment of each harmonic after matched filtering of the modulated signal is related to the target position, and it is unable to determine the harmonic order by the output signal of single-order matched filter. A multi-order matched filter network is used to solve the problem of ambiguous correspondence between pulse peak and harmonic order. The output signal model of multi-order matched filters is established and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Dual-Band and Dual-Polarized Millimeter-Wave Leaky-Wave Antenna
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-band and dual-polarized leaky-wave antenna based on corrugated substrate integrated waveguide (CSIW) at millimeter-wave band. The periodic open stubs work as the spoof surface plasmon polariton (SPP) mode at lower frequencies, and they will become the equivalent shorting vias for the half SIW mode at higher frequencies. Due to the SPP and SIW modes, the CSIW transmission line can operate in dual band. By loading periodic elements along both sides of the CSIW, it can achieve dual-band and dual-polarized leaky-wave radiation. In 22-28GHz band, the radiation beam scans from -13° to +30° with horizontal polarization, and the polarization state will become vertical with -21° ∼ +8° scanning range in 52-66 GHz.

articleTitle: What is the Nyquist Sampling Frequency for Amplitude-Only Planar Near-Field Tests?
abstract: It was claimed in the previous literature that the Nyquist sampling frequency must be doubled in the planar near-filed range if the phase information is not available. This paper discusses the Nyquist sampling interval for the amplitude-only planar near-field test. The spectrums of the complex and phaseless signals in wavenumber domain are discussed and analyzed. The half wavelength is shown to be a sufficient condition for the Nyquist sampling of phaseless planar near-field test, which is experimentally verified.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Chip to Waveguide Transition for W-band Wireless Transmission with Wire-Bonding
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost chip to waveguide transition for W-band wireless transmission. The wideband tran-sition between rectangular waveguide and substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) is realized by an SIW-fed cavity-backed patch antenna. On-chip ground-signal-ground (GSG) pads to SIW transition is then investigated by a compensated wire-bonding network with a grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW). The full transition is demonstrated by a W -band SiGe transmitter with an average of 3 dB loss within 75–100 GHz frequency range compared to on-wafer measurement results.

articleTitle: Crossed-Dipole-Shaped Metasurface Transmissive Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
abstract: This paper presents a single-layer wideband linear-to-circular (LTC) polarization converter implemented with a crossed-dipole-shaped metasurface. The LTC polarization converter is placed on the top side of a single-substrate layer. The proposed design yields a nearly equal transmission amplitude and steady phase difference of nearly 90° between the two orthogonal components of electromagnetic waves transmitted across a wide frequency range. The numerical results demonstrate that the polarizer can accomplish wideband LTC polarization conversion at both x- and y-polarized incident waves within a frequency range of 12.1–30.2 GHz, which represents a fractional bandwidth of 85.6%. Furthermore, the proposed LTC polarization converter achieves a high total transmittance of electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Wide Beamwidth Multi-Band Circularly Polarized Quadrifilar Helix Antenna with Multi-Coil Arms
abstract: A wide beamwidth multi-band quadrifilar helix antenna (QHA) is proposed. The proposed antenna operates in four bands, including GPS L1, XW-L and RDSS. This capability is achieved by introducing multiple resonances and incorporating a smaller parasitic QHA within the driven QHA. The external larger QHA has two helical arms, generating two closely band operating in a lower frequency band (1500-1700MHz) and a higher frequency band(2770-2840MHz). The internal smaller QHA operates in a higher frequency band(2410-2560MHz). Therefore, the proposed QHA covers four bands and exhibits a high frequency ratio of 1.85. In addition, the proposed QHA exhibits wide beamwidth, making it well-suited for satellite communication and navigation applications.

articleTitle: A Multifunctional Reflectarray Based on Resistance Modulation
abstract: A broadband metasurface with phase and amplitude modulation is proposed in this paper. The unit comprises four distinct quarter-round patches and four variable resistors that effectively reflect and absorb electromagnetic waves through the manipulation of resistor values. Amplitude and phase control are achieved by adjusting the resistance values of these variable resistors. When utilized as an absorber, the absorption rate exceeds 90%. As a 1-bit phase manipulation element, it achieves a 180° phase response within the ultra-wideband operating range of 14.3-28.7 GHz. A full-wave simulation of a reflectarray with 30×30 elements is performed to confirm beam control performance under different operating polarizations. The proposed element offers a multitude of functions, making it suitable for various situations.

articleTitle: A GaN MMIC Inverse Class-F Power Amplifier Using Co-Designed Bias Network and LC Resonator
abstract: This paper proposed a novel methodology to design compact and fully integrated inverse class-F (class-F-1) power amplifier (PA). In this method, a bias network (BN) is utilized to provide alternated open-circuit and short-circuit harmonic impedances and assist with fundamental matching. Then, a matching network (MN) formed by a parallel LC resonator is adopted to achieve isolation at 2nd harmonic and simultaneously help with impedance transformation at fundamental frequency. To validate the proposed method, a high efficiency class-F-1 PA operating at 5.8 GHz is designed using a commercial 0.25 μm GaN-on-SiC technology. Simulation results indicate that the proposed class-F-1 PA can provide a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 71% at saturation output power of 36.5 dBm.

articleTitle: A Wideband Vivaldi Antenna with Modified Planar Marchand Balun for mmWave V2X Communications
abstract: This paper presents the design and character-ization of a wideband Vivaldi antenna for millimeter-wave (mmWave) vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications. The antenna is designed to work at the frequency range of 24.25 GHz to 27.50 GHz (n258) tagged for fifth-generation (5G) mmWave. A planar Marchand balance-unbalance (balun), which was modified to suit a 50–Ω SMA connector avoiding bandwidth degradation, is used to feed the proposed antenna. The configuration is optimized to achieve an optimal design prior prototyping. Based on the optimization, a prototype of Vivaldi antenna is realized for experimental characterization. The result show that the realized antenna works well at the desired frequency range with the bandwidth achievement of 6.1 GHz from the frequency of 23.9 GHz to 30 GHz. In such frequency range, the gain is relatively constant, while the far-field radiation pattern indicates a directional nature.

articleTitle: Accurate and Efficient Computation for Irregular Reflectarray Antenna
abstract: Equivalent scattering matrix model on the fullarray level is applied to reflectarray antenna computation, and the antenna radiation patterns can be analyzed in milliseconds with almost invisible error against full-wave computations. The computation is started from the full-wave computed data for once, and then the antenna optimization can be highly accelerated. Notably, the reflectarray modelling is on the fullarray level and no longer depends on the local periodicity condition. Therefore, it can be used to arbitrary reflectarray antenna designs including conformal, sparse, thinned, sharedaperture cases where the periodicity is not well satisfied. An irregular reflectarray antenna, with irregular carrier shape, non-periodic and sparse array arrangement, different elements, poor polarization purity, polarization and impedance mismatched feed, is constructed, and the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method are well validated in comparison with full-wave computations.

articleTitle: A Wideband Bowtie Antenna Fed with CPW for 5G mmWave Applications
abstract: In recent years, millimeter wave (mmWave) antennas have garnered considerable attention, especially in the realm of 5G applications. This study introduces a compact wideband planar bowtie antenna designed specifically for 5G mmWave communications. The antenna consists of a pair of bowtie patches that are fed by a grounded co-planar waveguide (GCPW). Notably, this design requires only two thin substrate layers. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna offers a broad bandwidth of 33.35% (34.62–47.96 GHz) and achieves a realized gain of 6.25 dBi at 40 GHz.

articleTitle: On The Possibility of Polarization Switching for 5G mmWave Antenna
abstract: Wireless communications in millimeter-wave (mmWave) spectrum are being recognized as a promising approach in offering the possibility of achieving multi-gigabit data rates and opening up new opportunities for a variety of applications, including advancements beyond 5G communication. While in wireless communication systems, a switch-able polarized antenna is required to minimize multi path fading losses and enhance signal transmission performance by reducing polarization mismatch and interference with other systems. This paper deals with the design of an antenna with polarization switching capabilities which is intended for 5G wireless communication in the millimeter-wave spectrum. This antenna has the ability to switch the polarization from circular polarization to linear polarization and vice versa. The proposed antenna is designed by using Rogers RT/du<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>oid 5880 dielectric substrate with the relative permittivity of 2.2 and the thickness measuring 0.8 mm, while the connection method for the antenna is using a coaxial probe.

articleTitle: Improved Resolution for a 1-Bit Transmitarray in Near-Field Focusing Applications
abstract: We introduce a novel approach for enhancing the resolution of conventionall-bit transmitarrays (TAs) by utilizing space-time coding technology. Conventional l-bit TAs suffer from the relatively large focal spot due to the phase quantization issue. In this study, space-time modulation technology is introduced with the emergence of spatial harmonic components. By introducing a time delay index to the + 1 st harmonic wave, a continuous phase compensation could be achieved without impacting the original amplitude distribution, thereby achieving a smaller focal spot. Moreover, as the element number reduces (e.g., from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12\times 12,8\times 8$</tex>, and further to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a 6\times 6$</tex> array), the contrast between the near-field focal spots of the conventional l-bit TA and its + 1 st harmonic wave becomes increasingly pronounced. This method holds potential for low-cost and high-resolution imaging applications.

articleTitle: A 35-GHz Planar Aperture Rectenna for Wireless Power Transimission
abstract: A novel rectenna utilizing low-cost PCB process with high RF-to-dc conversion efficiency at 35 GHz is proposed. The receiving antenna is a planar aperture antenna with a simple structure, featuring a high gain of more than 15 dBi. By prolonging the antenna aperture and adopting a multi-section patch to block the region where the aperture electric field is reversed, the uniformity of the magnitude and phase of aperture field is improved and the aperture efficiency is enhanced. A class-F rectifier is printed on the back of the antenna and connected the antenna through slot coupling so compact integration of antenna and rectifying circuit without extra connectors is achieved. A prototype is fabricated and measured. When the incident power density is 13.4 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 35 GHz, the measured peak RF-to-dc conversion efficiency and output dc power are 52.3% and 46.8 mW, respectively.

articleTitle: The Influence of Calibration Materials' Dielectric Properties on Deembedding Accuracy for Liquid Characterization
abstract: The calibration and de-embedding outcomes of utilizing different liquid combinations as standards are studied. Using standards with significant disparities aids in minimizing calibration errors, whereas employing standards with similar liquid dielectric constants creates significant calibration discrepancies. Optimal calibration liquids consist of a high permittivity liquid, a low permittivity liquid, and a liquid with a constant permittivity. Simulation results validate the aforementioned findings.

articleTitle: A Novel Flexible Broadband Transmission Line with Low Loss
abstract: A novel flexible broadband transmission line enabling extremely low loss is proposed in this paper, which is composed of conductor-backed coplanar waveguide (CBCPW) and periodically arranged triangles at the edges. From theoretical simulation, it is demonstrated that the periodically arranged edge-based triangular arrays can effectively block wave leakage at DC-60 GHz. The design is simple and transmits the TEM mode. The flexible transmission line was verified for both flat and bent states, showing excellent transmission performance. It is observed that the average <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex> is −1.52 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}$</tex>, and the average <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{s}_{11}$</tex> is less than −10 dB in the whole band from DC to 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna Array With Dual Polarization Using Metasurface Absorber
abstract: The paper presents a novel dual-polarized base-station antenna array with 700-MHz and 3.6-GHz wideband elements in one shared radiating aperture. It comprises a magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna in 0.644-0.967 GHz (40.1 %), four dipole antennas in 3.29-5.18 GHz (44.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and a metasurface absorber. These four 3.6-GHz antennas are placed above the 700-MHz antenna. To suppress the mutual coupling between antenna elements working at different bands, a wideband metasurface absorber is placed below the 700-MHz antenna. The designed absorber is used to absorb the upper-band wave from the 700-MHz antenna, and works as a normal reflector for the lower-band electromagnetic wave. As a result, the proposed dual-polarized base-station antenna array has standard broadside radiation patterns in dual operating bandwidths.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Sleeve Loaded Dielectric Rod Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a new high-gain dielectric rod antenna (DRA) operating in the Ka-band is proposed. By adding a dielectric sleeve to the radiating structure of the DRA, the surface wave distribution on the DRA is altered and the aperture size is enlarged, realizing a high-gain performance DRA. The new high-gain DRA is fed by a rectangular metal waveguide and the impedance matching is achieved by a dovetail cone structure. The antenna operates at 26-40 GHz with a maximum gain of 21dBi. Compared to a conventional DRA, this antenna has an increase in gain of 3dB at the same height (6λ) despite an increase in cross-sectional size of 1.8λ. In addition, this paper proposed a way to achieve uniform signal strength coverage in a ground area by using the novel high-gain DRA.

articleTitle: On the Gap between the Amplitude and Phase Modulation Layers in a Transmitarray Collimator
abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) testing has become more and more popular in the communication device industry, especially for streamline product measurements. Because of its low profile and ease of manufacturing, transmitarray-based compact antenna test range (CATR) systems can be quite appropriate for cost-effective and efficient measurements. The CA TR collimator features two metasurface layers that incorporate phase modulation functions and magnitude modification functions, respectively. The collimator's performance is influenced by the gap length that exists between the two metasurfaces. The theoretical analysis of the gap effect is shown, and an optimization technique is proposed to improve the quiet zone's quality. The final transmitarray-based CATR achieves a high aperture ratio of 60%.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Demonstration of a Low-Profile Differential-Fed Tri-Band Filtering Antenna
abstract: The design and validation of a novel low-profile, differential-fed tri-band filtering antenna are demonstrated. The design consists of a driven patch and two pairs of parasitic strips. Four commensal stubs are added to the driven patch to improve the rate of attenuation at the band edge of the second working frequency band. Additionally, split-ring slots and shorted parasitic strips are appropriately incorporated to tailor the reflection coefficient and enhance the bandwidth of the corresponding working band. Overall, the antenna has a low profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.03\lambda_{1}$</tex> and a small footprint, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.09\lambda_{1^{2}}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{1}$</tex> represents the wavelength associated with the central frequency of the first operating band. Measurements of its prototype confirmed the same polarization direction and similar radiation properties over the tri-band antenna's operating frequency ranges of 2.4-2.487 GHz, 3.72-3.93 GHz, and 5.57-5.88 GHz. Because the antenna is built in a single-layer configuration, it and its operating bands can be easily scaled up to millimeter wave and even terahertz frequencies for related applications.

articleTitle: Cryogenic Receiver Frontends of High Sensitivity for Terahertz Communication Applications
abstract: This paper overviews our latest achievement in developing high-sensitivity cryogenic heterodyne receivers for terahertz (THz) wireless communication system applications. As typical representatives, one 220-GHz antenna-coupled cryogenic Schottky receiver and one 340-GHz high-temperature superconducting Josephson-junction heterodyne receiver, are both discussed in detail. Both cryogenic receivers have exhibited the superior performance, with their lowest single-sideband noise factors of around 4 dB and the intermediate-frequency (IF) bandwidths up to 20 GHz. Those achievement are attributed to innovative on-chip antenna and circuit designs as well as advanced device modelling and optimization methods. Those sensitive receiver frontends have been integrated into the THz communication systems for high-speed data transmission demonstrations.

articleTitle: Design of Fully Integrated GaN Dual-Band Doherty Power Amplifier for 5G Wireless Communication
abstract: The current study introduces the design and sim-ulation of a comprehensively integrated dual-band Doherty power amplifier (DPA), which employs Gallium Nitride (GaN) High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) technology for its fabrication. A specialized output matching network is designed for the carrier path to achieve dual-band Doherty operation. The overall circuit consists of a Wilkinson power divider, input matching networks, active devices and an output matching network and a phase shifter, all integrated onto a chip with a dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.60\times 3.05mm^{2}$</tex>. The fabricated DPA demonstrates operation at 3.5 GHz and 4.85 GHz with 6 dB high-efficiency power range. Following electromagnetic(EM) simulation, the designed DPA achieves a output back-off (OBO) drain efficiency exceeding 42%, a saturated drain efficiency exceeding 53%, and a peak output power of 37.5 dBm.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming Based on Space- Time Coding Metasurface Antenna with Hadamard Codes
abstract: A novel adaptive beamforming method utilizing the space-time coding metasurface and Hadamard codes is presented. By the modulation of the signal received by each element, the sum modulated signal can be received by single receiver. Then, the sum signal is used to reproduce each element's received signal. Ultimately, the reproduced signals are employed in adaptive beamforming, with the weighting vectors obtained from the traditional adaptive beamforming algorithm. Compared with the traditional adaptive beamforming method with digital array, the proposed method requires only single receiver, which greatly simplifies the receiver structure. In the end, the simulation proves the feasibility of the proposed adaptive beamforming method.

articleTitle: Generating Multi-Mode OAMs with Broadened Common Bandwidth Based on PIN Diodes-Loaded Archimedean Spiral Antenna
abstract: This paper proposes an Archimedean planar spiral antenna with PIN diodes loaded on the surface to generate multi-mode vortex electromagnetic (EM) waves. Due to the contributions of PIN diodes, the common bandwidth of different orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes is broadened. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna can generate vortex EM waves carrying four OAM modes with the common bandwidth of 1.8 GHz, which is of great significance for OAM applications.

articleTitle: A 220 GHz Mixer Based on Dual Circuit-Port Technique Utilizing Planar Schottky Diodes
abstract: In this study, we present a novel internal port assignment technique, known as the dual-circuit port (DCP) technique, applied for the design of sub-harmonic mixers utilizing planar Schottky diodes in the terahertz transceiver system. The DCP technique exhibits a consistent relationship between port numbers in the 3-D model and intrinsic model, offering clear physical meaning often neglected in conventional designs. Moreover, this technique enhances the accuracy of simulating the open state of planar Schottky diodes. To investigate the proposed DCP technique, a 220 GHz sub-harmonic mixer is designed based on planar Schottky barrier diodes. The simulation results of the mixer obtained from different internal port assignment techniques are compared.

articleTitle: A Wideband Metasurface Linear Polarization Converter
abstract: This paper presents a novel double U-shaped metasurface., which demonstrates remarkable capabilities in transforming y-polarized electromagnetic waves into x- polarized ones., and vice versa. Leveraging three distinct electric and magnetic resonances., this metasurface effectively broadens its operational bandwidth. The experimental findings remarkably corroborate the simulation results., demonstrating a polarization conversion ratio exceeding 90% across the frequency spectrum of (8.2-14.8) GHz.

articleTitle: Dual Gate HEMT: Compact Cascode for Low-Noise Amplification
abstract: The present work compares single-gate (SG) and dual-gate (DG) HEMTs from a low-noise amplification perspective. Experimental results, obtained through RF and noise measurements in the 5 to 50 GHz range, reveal a significant boost of ~6 dB in the associated gain for the DG-HEMT compared to the conventional SG-HEMT. The biasing characteristics of the DG-HEMT offer an additional degree of freedom, relaxing the traditionally rigid constraints on the relationship between minimum noise figure and gain.

articleTitle: Towards Porous SI THz Planar Waveguides in Ultra-Low-Resistivity Substrates
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to integrate a high-quality porous silicon (PSi) waveguide on ultra-low-resistivity (ULR) substrates for terahertz (THz) applications. Eliminating the need for deep etching and multiple wafer bonding, the proposed technique leverages the low resistivity of ULR substrate and the high resistivity of PSi to create an efficient waveguide. Simulations and preliminary experiments validate the concept.

articleTitle: G-Band Load-Pull Characterization of High-Efficiency Emitter-Fin InP/GaAsSb DHBTs
abstract: We report the small- and large-signal results of 250 nm InP/GaAsSb Double Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors (DHBTs) in G-band. We characterized the frequency behavior of the saturated output power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OUT,SAT</inf> and of power-added efficiency (PAE) in class-A operation. At 140 GHz, we find P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OUT,SAT</inf> = 11.1 dBm with a simultaneous record PAE = 39.2%. Together with the smallsignal cutoff frequencies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>/f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> > 0.48/1.1 THz, these data demonstrate the suitability of InP/GaAsSb DHBTs for highpower and high-efficiency sub-mm power amplifiers (PA).

articleTitle: A Broadband 1-Bit Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna for 5G millimeter Wave
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband 1-bit diode-loaded reflectarray, employing a quasi-magneto-electric (quasi-ME) dipole framework. By toggling the pin diodes between “ON” and “OFF” states, the element achieves a substantial 1-bit bandwidth spanning from 19.9 GHz to 30.5 GHz (42.06%) while maintaining a reflection phase difference within ±20° of 180°. Utilizing this proposed element, a prototype is manufactured and evaluated, demonstrating impressive beam scanning capabilities. The prototype achieves a peak gain of 22.5 dBi and a peak aperture efficiency of 22.6%. Notably, within a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 39.5% (21.8 – 31.8 GHz), showcasing the potential for advanced reconfigurable antenna systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Spearhead-Shaped Antenna with Super- Wideband Characteristics
abstract: This paper discusses the performance of a com-pact spearhead-shaped antenna (CSSA) with super-wideband characteristics. There are two types of groundplane configu-ration implemented for the antenna: (i) on Antenna I, using a flat partial groundplane (FPGP), and (ii) on Antenna II, using a spline-curved groundplane (SCGP). The spline used is a quadratic spline, composed of 13 control points (CPs) arranged symmetrically so that only 7 CPs have their position controlled in the configuration. From the measurement results, Antenna I with FPGP operates from the frequency of 3.66 GHz to 43.5 GHz or with the geometrical bandwidth of 315.7% and the bandwidth ratio of 11.89:1. Furthermore, improvements are achieved when using SCGP, Antenna II works from the frequency of 3.62 GHz to 43.5 GHz or with the geometrical bandwidth of 317.8% and the bandwidth ratio of 12.02:1.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Omnidirectional Radiation
abstract: In this paper, a wideband omnidirectional dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed. The antenna contains a tri-mode dielectric resonator (DR), which is fed by a coaxial probe. The TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> modes can be excited at the same time to enhance the bandwidth. The proposed antenna operating at 13.25–21.32 GHz exhibits a simulated −10dB impedance matching bandwidth of 46.7% and a stable omnidirectional radiation pattern over the whole working bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Omnidirectional Antenna-in-Package Based on FOWLP for THz Chip-to-Chip Wireless Interconnect Applications
abstract: This paper proposes an omnidirectional antenna-in-package (AiP) for THz chip-to-chip (C2C) wireless interconnect applications, based on fan-out wafer-level package (FOWLP). The microstrip monopolar patch antenna with 8 conductive vias is designed to motivate the TM01 pattern for achieving omnidirectional radiation and low profile, while additional directors are used to enhance the azimuthal plane gain. The meta-surface under the packaging mold is designed to decrease gain variation. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna achieves an impedance band of -10 dB in the 216-231 GHz range. Additionally, within 220-230 GHz, the antenna can achieve a peak azimuthal plane gain of 2.7 dBi and gain variation is lower than 3 dB. This antenna provides a feasible solution for future terahertz C2C wireless interconnect applications.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual-Polarization End-Fire Dielectric Resonator Antenna
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm-wave) dual-polarization end-fire dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented in this paper. The dielectric resonator (DR) and its feeding circuits are integrated on a single substrate. Horizontal and vertical polarizations are achieved by generating in-phase and out-of-phase signals with two pairs of feeding strips, respectively. To obtain a wide overlapping bandwidth of the two polarizations, a U-shaped parasitic structure featuring two strips and a via is designed between the two feeding strips. The simulated results show an overlapping bandwidth of 5.58% (37.8−40 GHz) and an isolation level more than 16 dB.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Dual-Channel Radar Transceiver in 22 nm CMOS with 60 GHz Bandwidth
abstract: This paper presents a 0.24-0.3 THz dual-channel broadband frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar transceiver in 22 nm CMOS. The proposed channel-switching strategy enables it to achieve a 60 GHz operation bandwidth. It employs a monostatic structure based on the doubler-last and the mixer-first architecture, eliminating the necessity for power-hungry local oscillator (LO) distribution circuit and lossy duplexers, resulting in a compact footprint and low power consumption. While consuming 270 m W power, the proposed transmitter (TX) achieves a peak output power (Pout) of -3.1 dBm, the receiver's (RX) maximum conversion gain (CG) is up to 7.2 dB, and the minimum noise figure (NF) is 30.5 dB at an intermediate frequency (IF) of 1 MHz. The Pout, CG, and NF values fluctuate by only 1.2, 2.3 and 3.1 dB, respectively, across the 60 GHz chirp bandwidth. The chip occupies a core area of 0.93 mm2.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Bandpass Mode-Composite Cavity Filter With Large Frequency Ratio
abstract: A novel dual-mode-composite (DMC) cavity resonator is proposed. The DMC cavity is fulfilled based on a rectangular waveguide (RW) cavity by introducing an array of periodic metallic pins into it. Benefiting the introduced periodic metallic pins, the electromagnetic band-gap structures (EBGs) are formed in the DMC cavity and two TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf>-like modes are excited in it. By cascading the DMC cavity resonators, a dual-band filter is designed with three millimeter-wave (mm-wave) band filtering channels and one microwave-band filtering channel.

articleTitle: Optimization Design Methodology for High Efficiency Power Amplifiers
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization design method for high efficiency power amplifier (PA). In order to enhance the operational efficiency and streamline the design process of the PA, a sinusoidal adaptive simulated annealing particle swarm optimization is proposed to achieve compre-hensive optimization of the PA's efficiency, output power, and gain, which avoids the unexpected performance degradation caused by conventional high efficiency PA designs methodologies. To validate the proposed method, four high efficiency PAs operating at 0.5, 1.5, 2.2, and 3.5 GHz were designed optimized. Furthermore, the high efficiency PA operating at 1.5 GHz was implemented and measured. The measured results show an 80% drain efficiency is achieved at saturated output power of 41 dBm.

articleTitle: A Gain Filtering Reflectarray Unit Based on 1-Bit Magnetoelectric Dipole
abstract: This paper presents a reflectarray (RA) unit with gain filtering characteristic based on 1-bit magnetoelectric (ME) dipole. The reflection element comprises a pair of ME dipole, a ground plane and a feeding arm. By integrating the split branches into the ME dipole, the operation bandwidth of the cell is limited to 8.7-14.16 GHz (with |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| <-10 dB), enabling effective out-of-band suppression. By adjusting the length of the feeding arm, the antenna unit can achieve different phase delays of 0° and 180°. Finally, the simulated results demonstrate that this RA antenna unit offers wide bandwidth and superior out-ofband gain suppression.

articleTitle: FMCW Detection Based on Harmonic Characteristic Analysis Method without Velocity-direction Coupling
abstract: A novel Frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar detection method based on harmonic characteristic analysis using 1-bit time modulated array (TMA) is proposed. The signal model and no frequency aliasing condition are derived. The estimation methods for range, velocity and direction are proposed. Compared to switched antenna arrays (SAA) with one element excited at the same time, 1-bit TMA with all elements excited simultaneously can improve echo efficiency. By designing the harmonic directional pattern of the 1-bit TMA to meet the amplitude comparison method direction finding conditions, direction finding results are unrelated to the phase of echo signal, thus solving the velocity direction coupling problem. Simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: D-Band Dual-Polarized Array Antenna based on Turnstile-Junction Orthomode Transducer with High Isolation
abstract: This paper presents a D-band dual-polarized array antenna (DP AA) for sub-terahertz application. The proposed DPAA, derived from turnstile-junction orthomode transducer (OMT), inherently possesses high isolation characteristics due to the symmetric architecture and dual differential excitation. High cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) in E- and H-planes for both polarizations is another superior property. Several key components, including E-plane T -junction, power divider, parallel-plated waveguide, cross slot array, and metal stepped post are designed to constitute the DPAA. A simulated prototype of the DPAA exhibits a −10-dB impedance bandwidth ranging from 133.8 GHz to 147.1 GHz, with isolation exceeding 54 dB within band. Moreover, the XPD is better than 40 dB for both polarizations, and the maximum realized gain reaches up to 26.2 dBi at 144.5 GHz.

articleTitle: An Integrated Sensing and Communication Architecture using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for 6G Wireless Networks
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), known for their wave manipulation capability, are emerging as a key technology for future wireless networks, especially with the integration of sensing and communication (ISAC) functionalities. The proposed architecture based on RIS offers passive sensing and communication capabilities. It combines frequency-diverse compressed sensing and wide-angle beam-forming techniques to demonstrate dual functions: it can precisely detect passive objects and enhance wireless signals using quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). Its precision in detecting passive objects comes with an error margin of less than 1.5 cm. In terms of wireless signal enhancement, the RIS boosts signals by 8 dB in the 15 to 21 GHz frequency range. Its dual functionality in precise passive detection and signal enhancement, these features make the RIS highly relevant for sixth-generation (6G) applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Special-shaped Reflector on Antenna Radiation Pattern and FBR
abstract: The reflector is one of the most important components of the antenna, and the shape of the reflector has a great effect on many parameters of the antenna, especially the radiation pattern and the front-to-back ratio (FBR). In this paper, the influence of different shapes of reflectors of the antenna is analyzed by taking the dual-polarized crisscross-shaped dipole antenna with coupling feed as an example. The antenna is designed to operate in the band of 0.69-0.96GHz (with S11<-10 dB), which can cover the lower frequency band of 5G communication. After analysis, compared with the most commonly used flat reflector, the bending-typed reflector can increase the FBR by 10dB, and the circular groove shaped reflector can increase the FBR by 15dB. At the same time, the operating frequency band and radiation pattern of the antenna remains basically stable.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Transmitarray Antenna with Linearly Polarized Feed
abstract: This paper presents a receiving-transmitting (R-T) topology scheme based on a novel differentially-transferred unit cell. The middle metallic layer as the common ground. The uppermost metallic layer comprises of a pair of spiral strips for transmitting. For demonstration, a simple linearly polarized (LP) horn antenna is utilized to illuminate the transmitarray comprising 20 X 20 differential elements. The measured results of the fabricated prototype are in alignment with the simulated ones. The measured 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 60.9% (17-31.8 GHz) and the 3-dB gain bandwidth is 43.9% (19.65-30.4 GHz).

articleTitle: A Two-Chip-Cascaded 4D Millimeter-Wave Imaging Radar Aiming for Automotive SLAM
abstract: Since the concept of simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) was proposed and investigated in 1980s, it has been attracting continuous attentions not only from classic robotics regime but also from extended virtual reality (VR)/amplified reality (AR), unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and autonomous driving applications, respectively. This paper focuses on a SLAM oriented solution merely using millimeter-wave 4D imaging radar for autonomous parking function. The two-chip cascaded 4D radar offers totally 6 transmitting and 8 receiving physic channels in RF front-end. By applying sparse antenna array and multi-input multi-output (MIMO) technique, 48 virtual channels can be emulated, which achieve angle separation each of 1.5°on azimuth and 3°on elevation plane. With maximum detection range of 306 m, the implemented 4D radar can demonstrate reasonable imaging effect aiming for SLAM application by generating 10240 points/s in various on-vehicle low-speed outdoor test scenarios.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effects of the Slot Parameters on a Patch Antenna at 28 GHz Related to the Operating Wavelength
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the effects of the slots etched on a square patch antenna on the radiation characteristics related to the operatingwavelength at 28 GHz. We first design an inset fed patch antenna with a square geometry operating at 28 GHz. Then we etch a rhombic shaped slot in the middle point of the patch and perform a parametric analysis for the edge dimensions of 1/10, 1/100 and 1/1000 of the wavelength. Additionally, we move the slot along the vertical axis with the distances from the center of 1/10, 1/100 and 1/1000 of the wavelength and analyze the effects. Finally, after etching additional slots on the bottom edges of the antenna and shift them in +y direction we acquire extra bandwidth and lower return loss levels. With this final desigR we reach at an increase for the bandwidth of 180 MHz and a reduction of 25.51 dB for reflection coefficient level. These novel features yield the proposed structure a suitable model for 5G communications and it can clearly be concluded that there is a strong relationship between the antenna characteristics and slot parameters related to the operating wavelength.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Filtering Fabry-Pérot Cavity Antenna utilizing PRFS
abstract: This paper introduces a filtering technique applying to the Fabry-Pérot Cavity (FPC) antenna for millimeter-wave (mmw) application. The proposed antenna is made up of FPC and partially-reflective-and-filtering surface (PRFS). The PRFS not only produces filtering response but also provides partially reflective surface (PRS) of waves. The designed antenna has both high-gain and filtering characteristics without increasing the overall profile and complexity, so it is a good candidate for millimeter wave applications. To demonstrate the design concept, we designed and fabricated a high-gain filter antenna operating at 30 GHz using PCB technology. The simulation results show that the antenna has good impedance matching in 29.5 GHz - 31.5 GHz, and the out-of-band suppression level is greater than 15 dB. The maximum gain of the antenna is 16.9dBi, and the flatness of the in-band gain is less than 4dB.
